rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy reported that God ordered the Prophet to recite the opening of al-Bayyina to him, followed by statements identifying the true religion as non-polytheist hanifiyya and promising that good is not denied.
rows.anchor: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك فقرأ علي

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A second Ubayy report presents an expanded recitation with explanations of upright religion, righteous deeds, the best and worst of creation, and the recompense of the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: إن أقوم الدين الحنيفية مسلمة غير مشركة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recalled the Prophet's saying that Adam would seek a third valley of gold after two, and that only dust fills his belly; God accepts repentance.
rows.anchor: لو كان لابن آدم واديان من ذهب لابتغى الثالث

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy affirmed that the Prophet had taught him the disputed wording; Umar asked whether to enter it in the codex, and Ubayy did not forbid him.
rows.anchor: هكذا اقرأنيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Ubayy quoted the two-valley saying, and Umar asked whether it should be written; Ubayy said he would not forbid it, while remaining unsure whether it was revelation or Prophetic speech.
rows.anchor: فكأن أبيا شك أقول من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قرآن منزل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid said that when the surah was revealed, God told the Prophet to recite it to Ubayy, who asked whether God had commanded this and agreed when told yes.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glossed منفكين as ceasing their state, the Bayyina as this Qur'an, and the purified pages as the Qur'an praised in the finest terms.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين} قال: منتهي عما هم فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada described hanifiyya as the final dispensation, including forbidden close kin and rites; the religion of right standing is what God sent, prescribed, and approved.
rows.anchor: والحنيفية الختام وتحريم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Saeed attributed to the Prophet the statement that Ali is the best of creation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد مرفوعا: علي خير البرية

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reported that companions of the Prophet would say, whenever Ali approached, that the best of creation had come.
rows.anchor: فكان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أقبل علي قالوا: جاء خير البرية

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identified the Bayyina as Muhammad and glossed دين القيمة as the upright religion.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {حتى تأتيهم البينة} قال: محمد وفي قوله: {وذلك دين القيمة} قال: القيم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identified the Bayyina that came to the People of the Book as Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة} قال: محمد

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: When challenged on whether prayer and almsgiving belong to faith, al-Zuhri answered by citing the command to worship sincerely, pray, and give alms.
rows.anchor: قلت للزهري تزعمون أن الصلاة والزكاة ليس من الإيمان فقرأ {وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah argued that prayer and almsgiving are part of religion because the verse includes them among what people were commanded to do.
rows.anchor: فالصلاة والزكاة من الدين

rows.speaker: أبو واثل
rows.claim: Abu Wa'il answered questions about faith by reciting the passage from the disbelievers of the Book through sincere worship.
rows.anchor: كان أبو واثل إذا سئل عن شيء من الإيمان قرأ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra said a believer's standing with God on Judgment Day exceeds that of an angel, citing the believers who are the best of creation.
rows.anchor: لمنزلة العبد المؤمن عند الله يوم القيامة أعظم من منزلة ملك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet answered Aisha's question about the most honored creatures by pointing to the verse on believers who do righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: يا عائشة أما تقرئين {إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك هم خير البرية}

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reported the Prophet swearing that Ali and his followers would triumph on Judgment Day; the verse was revealed, and companions called Ali the best of creation.
rows.anchor: إن هذا وشيعته لهم الفائزون يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ali that he and his followers are the best of creation and will be pleased and pleasing on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: هو أنت وشيعتك يوم القيامة راضين مرضيين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reported that the Prophet identified him and his followers as the best of creation, promising their meeting at the Pool, where they will appear radiant among nations summoned for judgment.
rows.anchor: أنت وشيعتك وموعدي وموعدكم الحوض إذا جئت الأمم للحساب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reported that al-Zalzala was revealed in Medina; Qatada independently also classified it as Medinan.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة {إذا زلزلت} بالمدينة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A man with old age, a hard heart, and a heavy tongue asked for a comprehensive surah; the Prophet recited al-Zalzala, and the man said it sufficed him.
rows.anchor: فأقرأه {إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها} حتى فرغ منها

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Anas says reciting al-Zalzala equals half the Qur'an, al-Ikhlas a third, and al-Kafirun a quarter.
rows.anchor: من قرأ {إذا زلزلت} عدلت له بنصف القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reported the same recitation equivalences: al-Zalzala counts as half, al-Ikhlas as a third, and al-Kafirun as a quarter of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {إذا زلزلت} تعدل نصف القرآن

rows.speaker: رجل من بني جهينة
rows.claim: A man of Juhayna was unsure whether the Prophet intentionally recited al-Zalzala in both dawn prayer units or did so accidentally.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من بني جهينة أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في الصبح {إذا زلزلت الأرض} في الركعتين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib reported that the Prophet recited al-Zalzala in both rak'as of dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بأصحابه الفجر فقرأ بهم في الركعة الأولى {إذا زلزلت الأرض} ثم أعادها

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reported that the Prophet prayed two seated rak'as after witr, reciting al-Zalzala and al-Kafirun.
rows.anchor: عن أبي امامة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ركعتين بعد الوتر وهو جالس يقرأ فيهما {إذا زلزلت}

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reported that after witr the Prophet recited the Opening and al-Zalzala in one seated rak'a, then al-Kafirun in the next.
rows.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي بعد الوتر ركعتين وهو جالس يقرأ في الركعة الأولى بأم الكتاب و {إذا زلزلت}

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi said that reciting al-Zalzala equals one sixth of the Qur'an, unlike reports in this chapter assigning it half.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: من قرأ {إذا زلزلت} فإنها تعدل سدس القرآن

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reported a saying that al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Qur'an, al-Zalzala half, and al-Kafirun a quarter.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم قال: كان يقال: (قل هو الله أحد) ثلث القرآن و {إذا زلزلت الأرض} نصف القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glossed the earth's shaking as movement from below, its burdens as the dead, the question as a disbeliever's, its speech as God's command, and people's departure as coming from everywhere.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس {إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها} تحركت من أسفلها {وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها} قال: الموتى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identified the earth's burdens as those in graves; it will tell people what they did upon it because God commanded it, and it will cast out its contents.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها} قال: من في القبور

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya glossed the earth's burdens as the treasures and dead within it.
rows.anchor: ما فيها من الكنوز والموتى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said the earth will disgorge gold and silver like pillars; murderers, kin-breakers, and thieves will identify the wealth tied to their crimes, then leave it untouched.
rows.anchor: تقيء الأرض أفلاذ كبدها أمثال الأسطوان من الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet explained that the earth's reports are its testimony against every man and woman, naming deeds and their dates as committed on its surface.
rows.anchor: فإن أخبارها أن تشهد على كل عبد أو أمة بما عمل على ظهرها

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet said the earth will report every deed done on it; Gabriel had told him it would recount every action when Judgment Day comes.
rows.anchor: خبرها إذا كان يوم القيامة أخبرت بكل عمل عمل على ظهرها

rows.speaker: ربيعة الجرشي
rows.claim: The Prophet urged people to guard themselves on earth, described as their mother, because it will report every good or evil deed done upon it.
rows.anchor: تحفظوا من الأرض فإنها أمكم وإنه ليس من أحد عامل عليها خيرا أو شرا

rows.speaker: الحكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakam explained that Abu Umayya moved around the Meccan mosque after reciting the verse so different places would testify for him on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فأردت أن تشهد لي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud's reading was يومئذ تنبئ أخبارها; the narrator also heard him read the standard wording تحدث أخبارها.
rows.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقرأ بقراءة ابن مسعود هذه الآية: يومئذ تنبئ أخبارها وقرأ مرة {يومئذ تحدث أخبارها}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glossed the people's departure in separate groups as their becoming divided.
rows.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله: {يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا} قال: فرقا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj glossed their departure as splitting apart into groups that will never again assemble, and called the surah uniquely comprehensive.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه {يومئذ يصدر الناس} قال: يتصدعون {أشتاتا} فلا يجتمعون بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr feared that even an atom's weight of evil would be shown, the Prophet said disliked worldly experiences repay evil deeds while good is preserved until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فبمثاقيل ذر بشر ويدخل لك مثاقيل ذر الخير حتى توفاه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أسماء
rows.claim: Asma reported Abu Bakr asking whether all his bad deeds would be shown; the Prophet said worldly hardships are recompense and good is stored for its people in the next life.
rows.anchor: ما ترون مما تكرهون فذاك مما تجزون به ويدخر الخير لأهله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr cried over the surah, the Prophet said God forgives people who sin; without their errors and forgiveness, God would create a people who sin and are forgiven.
rows.anchor: لولا أنكم تخطئون وتذنبون فيغفر لكم لخلق الله أمة يخطئون

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
rows.claim: The Prophet said good deeds receive their afterlife reward, evil deeds may be seen as worldly misfortunes or illnesses, and anyone possessing an atom of good enters Paradise.
rows.anchor: من عمل منكم خيرا فجزاؤه في الآخرة ومن عمل منكم شرا يراه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو إدريس الخولاني
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Bakr that disliked events are recompense for evil and good is saved for Judgment Day, citing the teaching that calamities come from people's deeds while God pardons much.
rows.anchor: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet affirmed that even major and minor deeds will be seen; good is multiplied tenfold to seven hundredfold, evil counts once or is forgiven, and salvation depends on God's mercy, even for him.
rows.anchor: فإن الحسنة بعشر أمثالها يعني إلى سبعمائة ضعف والله يضاعف لمن يشاء والسيئة بمثلها أو يعفو الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: After 76:8, some Muslims thought tiny gifts were unrewarded and others thought minor sins harmless; the verse encourages small good and warns that small evil can grow. ذر means the smallest ant, seen in one's record with joy.
rows.anchor: يرون أنهم لا يؤجرون على الشيء القليل إذا أعطوه فيجيء السائل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said believers and unbelievers alike are shown their good and evil: believers are forgiven some sins and rewarded for good, whereas unbelievers' good is rejected and their sins punished.
rows.anchor: فأما لمؤمن فيريه الله حسناته وسيئاته فيغفر له من سيئاته

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said an unbeliever's good is repaid in worldly family and wealth until death, while a believer experiences worldly punishment for sins and leaves life cleared of them.
rows.anchor: من يعمل مثقال ذرة من خير من كافر يرى ثوابها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: صعصعة بن معاوية
rows.claim: After the Prophet recited the two verses, Sa'sa'a ibn Mu'awiya said they sufficed him and he did not need to hear any more Qur'an.
rows.anchor: حسبي لا أبالي أن لا أسمع من القرآن غيرها

rows.speaker: المطلب بن عبد الله بن حنطب
rows.claim: A Bedouin asked whether the promise applied even to an atom's weight; the Prophet said yes, and his repeated exclamation showed that faith had entered his heart.
rows.anchor: فقال الأعرابي: يا رسول الله أمثقال ذرة قال: نعم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: When a man heard the verses and cried in dismay, the Prophet said that man had believed; Zayd also reports the man affirming the same point himself.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أما الرجل فقد آمن

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: A student stopped when he reached the promise that a particle of good is seen; the Prophet told the teacher to leave him because he had understood.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: دعه فقد فقه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada said a learner heard the whole passage and concluded that even an atom of good or evil would be seen, calling that enough for him.
rows.anchor: إن عملت مثقال ذرة من خيرا رأيته وإن عملت مثقال ذرة من شر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reported a Muslim's response to the verse: even an atom of good or evil would be seen, so the admonition was complete.
rows.anchor: إن عملت مثقال ذرة من خير أو شر رأيته انتهت الموعظة

rows.speaker: الحارث بن سويد
rows.claim: Al-Harith ibn Suwayd remarked that the verse's accounting is severe.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الإحصاء شديد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima said an unbeliever's record displays worldly good only for it to be rejected, citing 25:23; a believer receives his record in his right hand, sees sins forgiven, and rejoices, citing 25:70.
rows.anchor: فينظر فيه فيرى فيه كل حسنة عملها في الدنيا فترد عليه حسناته

rows.speaker: سليمان بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet said the good works of a father who died before Islam would not benefit him, but his kinship, fidelity, and hospitality would protect his descendants from disgrace, humiliation, and poverty.
rows.anchor: مات قبل الإسلام قال: نعم قال: لن ينفعه ذلك ولكنها تكون في عقبه

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda defined full piety as guarding against even doubtful lawful matters for fear of the forbidden, and urged people not to dismiss any evil or omit any good, however small.
rows.anchor: حتى يتقيه في مثقال ذرة حتى أن يترك بعض ما يرى أنه حلال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet said Paradise and Hell are closer to a person than his sandal strap, then recited the promise that every atom of good or evil will be seen.
rows.anchor: اعملو أن الجنة والنار أقرب إلى أحدكم من شراك نعله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reported the Prophet's instruction to guard against the Fire even with half a date; she then recited the verse about seeing every atom of good.
rows.anchor: اتقو النار ولو بشق تمرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reported that Aisha gave a beggar a single date, explaining that it contained many atom weights and that the people were numerous while God alone sufficed them.
rows.anchor: نعم والله إن الخلق كثير ولا يشبعه إلا الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha instructed her servant to give a beggar the only date available, since it contained atom weights of good if accepted.
rows.anchor: أعطيه إياها فإن فيها مثاقيل ذر إن تقبلت

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha gave a beggar one grape from a basket and said it outweighed many atoms, illustrating the verse.
rows.anchor: هذه أثقل من ذر كثير

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar gave a needy person one grape from a bunch, saying it contained many atom weights of good.
rows.anchor: وقال: فيه مثاقيل ذر كثيرة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: When others questioned his giving only one grape to a beggar, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said it contained many atom weights.
rows.anchor: فقال: في هذه مثاقيل ذر كثير

rows.speaker: سعد بن مالك
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Malik gave a beggar one date; when the beggar hesitated, he invoked acceptance of even an atom or mustard seed and noted the date held many atoms.
rows.anchor: تقبل الله منا مثقا الذرة والخردلة وكم في هذه من مثاقيل الذر

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddad contrasted the transient world, shared by righteous and wicked, with the deferred afterlife under a mighty king: good belongs wholly in Paradise and evil in Hell; he cited the verses.
rows.anchor: ألا وإن الخير بحذافيره في الجنة ألا وإن الشر بحذافيره في النار

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: When a beggar criticized receiving one date from the Prophet, he replied that it contained many atom weights of good.
rows.anchor: أما علمت أن فيها مثاقيل ذر كثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas illustrated the atom's weight by taking dust in his hand and blowing: every particle among them is an atom's weight.
rows.anchor: أدخل يده في التراب ثم رفعها ثم نفخ فيها

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddad urged people to live for the afterlife, remain wary before God, expect their deeds to be displayed, and remember that every atom of good or evil will be seen.
rows.anchor: اعملوا وأنتم من الله على حذر واعملوا أنكم معرضون على أعمالكم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said horses belong to three owners: one earns reward, one gains protection, and one bears sin; asked about donkeys, he cited only this comprehensive verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الخيل لثلاثة: لرجل أجر ولرجل ستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked about donkeys, the Prophet said no revelation addressed them beyond this uniquely comprehensive rule about every atom of good and evil.
rows.anchor: ما نزل علي فيها إلا هذه الآية الجامعة الفاذة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explained the syntax as fronted wording: the intended order says God witnesses against the human being, and the human is intensely attached to wealth.
rows.anchor: هذه من مقاديم الكلام يقول وإن الله على ذلك لشهيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glossed الخير, “good,” here as wealth.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة {وإنه لحب الخير} قال: هو المال

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said a person testifies against himself; the graves are opened when people are raised, and what lies in hearts is brought out.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} قال: الإنسان شاهد على نفسه {أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما في القبور}

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet warned against people who pit Qur'anic passages against each other and follow ambiguities to claim a path concerning God; it likens them to the nation's Magi, the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: أناس من أمتي يضربون القرآن بعضه ببعض ليبطلوه ويتبعون ما تشابه

rows.speaker: الذهبي
rows.claim: Al-Dhahabi noted that Abu Hatim weakened al-Bukhturi and others faulted the report; Abu Nuaym said al-Bukhturi narrated fabricated material from his father.
rows.anchor: قال الذهبي في الميزان: البختري ضعفه أبو حاتم وأعله غيره

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: In a story to Jesus, punished villagers said their crimes were obeying sinful leaders and loving worldly life as a child loves its mother, grieving its departure and neglecting obedience; they died together and were cast into Sijjin.
rows.anchor: ما كان جنايتكم قالوا عبادة الطاغوت وحب الدنيا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: One villager could speak because he had shared the community but not its way; he remained suspended over Hell unsure whether he would be thrown in or saved, and Jesus praised hardship with safety over worldly ease.
rows.anchor: إني كنت فيهم ولم أكن على حالهم فلما جاء البلاء عمني معهم

rows.speaker: أنصاري
rows.claim: An Anṣari became gravely ill after asking God to make any punishment due in the afterlife occur in this life when he heard the Prophet recite al-Qari'a through “a scorching Fire.”
rows.anchor: فقلت اللهم ما كان من ذنب أنت معذبي عليه في الآخرة فعجل لي عقوبته في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet visited a missing companion after three days, urged others to visit him, and heard that the man could retain nothing in his stomach after his prayer for immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: إذا فقد الرجل من إخوانه ثلاثة أيام سأل عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud glossed the blessing for which people will be questioned as security and health.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في الآية قال النعيم: الأمن والصحة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali gave two glosses for the questioned blessing: well-being, and ordinary comforts such as wheat bread, chilled Euphrates water, and a home.
rows.anchor: عن أكل خبز البر وشرب ماء الفرات مبردا وكان له منزل يسكنه

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: The Prophet described people among his community who would eat ghee and honey combined with fine flour as an example of worldly blessing.
rows.anchor: ناس من أمتي يعقدون السمن والعسل بالنقى فيأكلونه

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل الكتاب
rows.claim: A man of the People of the Book said God will question a servant even about the minimum sustenance, shade, and clothing provided to him.
rows.anchor: قدر ما يقيم به صلبه من الخبز وما يكنه من الظل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: When the Companions wondered what blessing they had amid barley bread and half-full stomachs, God instructed the Prophet to include shoes and cold water.
rows.anchor: أليس تحتذون النعال وتشربون الماء البارد فهذا من النعيم

rows.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
rows.claim: The Companions asked what blessing they could be questioned about when they had only dates and water, weapons at hand, and an enemy present; the Prophet said such plenty would come.
rows.anchor: عن أي نعيم نسأل وإنما هما الأسودان الماء والتمر وسيوفنا على رقابنا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A second report has people ask how they could be questioned while living on dates and water with swords on their shoulders and enemies present; the Prophet replied that this would come.
rows.anchor: عن أي النعيم نسأل وإنما هما الأسودان والعدو حاضر وسيوفنا على عواتقنا

rows.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
rows.claim: The Companions asked which blessing they would be questioned about when only dates and water were available; the Prophet said such blessings would come.
rows.anchor: وأي نعيم نسأل عنه وإنما هما الأسودان التمر والماء

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr repeated the report that people asked about questioning when only dates and water were their blessing, and the Prophet said greater blessings would come.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله أي نعيم نسأل عنه وإنما هما الأسودان الماء والتمر

rows.speaker: صفوان بن سليم
rows.claim: The Companions asked what blessing could be questioned when they had only water and dates with swords on their shoulders; the Prophet said there would be future plenty.
rows.anchor: عن أي نعيم نسأل إنما هما الأسودان الماء والتمر وسيوفنا على عواتقنا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reported that people asked the Prophet what blessing they could be questioned about while carrying their swords and facing hardship.
rows.anchor: أي نعيم نسأل عنه وسيوفنا على عواتقنا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The first question a servant will face about blessing is whether God kept his body healthy and gave him cold water to drink.
rows.anchor: ألم نصح لك جسمك ونروك من الماء البارد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet called health and free time two blessings in which many people are cheated.
rows.anchor: نعمتان مغبون فيهما كثير من الناس الصحة والفراغ

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani transmitted that the blessing asked about is a morsel to sustain a person, water to quench him, and clothing to cover him.
rows.anchor: كسرة تقوته وماء يرويه وثوب يواريه

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: After the Prophet and two Companions ate fresh dates and drank water at Jabir's home, the Prophet called that a blessing they would be asked about.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هذا النعيم الذي تسألون عنه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar said hunger led him to the mosque, where he met Abu Bakr and the Prophet; the three agreed they were driven by hunger and went to the home of Malik ibn al-Tayhan, Abu al-Haytham.
rows.anchor: والله ما أخرجنا إلا ما نجد في بطوننا من حاق الجوع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The hungry Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar were welcomed by Abu Ayyub, who served goat, dates, and water; after eating, the Prophet identified the meal as the blessing asked about at Judgment.
rows.anchor: والذي نفسي بيده إن هذا لهو النعيم الذي تسألون عنه

rows.speaker: محمد بن عباس
rows.claim: After eating, the Prophet taught that saying God's name before the meal and praising Him afterward makes the meal sufficient acknowledgment of its blessing.
rows.anchor: فإذا شيعتم فقولوا: الحمد لله الذي هو أشبعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham slaughtered a young goat for the Prophet and his companions; later, when Fatima asked for a helper, the Prophet gave the grateful host a boy from Yemen, who eventually was released and found a livelihood in Syria.
rows.anchor: فذبح ونصب فلم يلبث إذا جاء بذلك إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In Ibn Mas'ud's account of a meal at Abu al-Haytham's, a Companion called it a blessing to be questioned about; the Prophet replied that worldly hardship brings no reproach to a believer, only to an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: المؤمن لا يثرب عليه شيء أصابه في الدنيا إنما يثرب على الكافر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi restricted the questioning about blessing to unbelievers, citing 46:20; his report quotes the Prophet saying believers are not reproached for worldly experiences, while unbelievers are.
rows.anchor: إنما هي للكفار {أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا}

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi's account traces the claim about believers and unbelievers to al-Sha'bi, from al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud.
rows.anchor: قيل له من حدثك قال: الشعبي عن الحارث عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: Amir reported that after eating meat, bread, barley, dates, and drinking cold water, the Prophet swore that this was a blessing.
rows.anchor: أكل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر لحما

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet told people facing hunger and war that later generations would be questioned about plentiful meals, fine clothes, and ornate homes, while praising the Companions as better than them.
rows.anchor: أنتم خير منهم يغذي عليهم بجفنة ويراح عليهم بجفنة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A needy man asked whether he had any blessing; the Prophet said yes, including shade, sandals, and cold water.
rows.anchor: نعم الظل والنعلان والماء البارد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas listed repaired shoes, cold water, and broken bread as blessings for which people will be questioned; al-Abbas explained the shoe reference.
rows.anchor: الخصاف والماء والبارد وفلق الكسر قال العباس: الخصاف خصف النعلين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet said a garment above the waist, shade from a wall, and bread are blessings for which a servant will be accountable.
rows.anchor: ما فوق الإزار وظل الحائط وخبز يحاسب به العبد يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmitted a report that a servant is not accountable for shade, a crust of bread to sustain him, and a garment covering his nakedness.
rows.anchor: ظل خص يستظل به وكسرة يشد بها صلبه وثوب يواري به عورته

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman said he had heard a Torah saying that a person needs only a morsel, a rag for covering, and a stone for shelter.
rows.anchor: ابن آدم كسيرة تكفيك وخرقة تواريك وحجر يؤيك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr told a poor Emigrant with a wife and a home that he no longer belonged among the destitute Emigrants.
rows.anchor: ألك امرأة تأوي إليك وتأوي إليها

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: The Prophet said that beyond house-shade, coarse bread, clothing to cover nakedness, and water, a son of Adam has no further claim to anything.
rows.anchor: كل شيء سوى ظل بيت وجلف الخبز وثوب يواري عورته والماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said al-Fil was revealed in Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال: أنزل {ألم تر كيف فعل ربك} بمكة

rows.speaker: عثمان بن المغيرة بن الأخنس
rows.claim: A report on the Elephant army says Abraha, king of Yemen, marched with a large force after a church was plundered; tribes directed him toward the Kaaba, and he seized Abd al-Muttalib's camels.
rows.anchor: أن أبرهة الأشرم الحبشي كان ملك اليمن

rows.speaker: عثمان بن المغيرة بن الأخنس
rows.claim: Abd al-Muttalib asked only for his camels, telling Abraha the Sanctuary had a Lord to protect it; Abraha ordered the Kaaba destroyed and Mecca plundered, but the elephant balked and birds attacked.
rows.anchor: أما بنيتنا هذه وبلدنا هذه فإن لهما ربا إن شاء أن يمنعها منعهما

rows.speaker: عثمان بن المغيرة بن الأخنس
rows.claim: Birds like bats pelted the army with round stones that pierced bodies; Abd al-Muttalib's scouts found the army dead, while Shahr later lost limbs and died after fleeing.
rows.anchor: فرمتهم بحجارة مدحرجة كالبنادق تقع على رأس الرجل فتخرج من جوفه

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Abd al-Muttalib and his men recovered their property; his poem thanked God for protecting the army and elephants, and Shahr fled, gradually losing limbs before dying.
rows.anchor: أنت منعت الجيش والأفيالا وقد رعو بمكة الأفيالا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said the army camped at al-Safah; the elephant retreated from the House, and God sent birds with black, clay-coated stones that caused an itch and flesh to fall away.
rows.anchor: كانوا لا يقدمون فيلهم إلا تأخر فدعا الله الطير الأبابيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says Abraha meant to frighten the Meccans; Abd al-Muttalib prayed for the sanctuary, then birds pelted the army as the elephant bellowed and the men became eaten stalks.
rows.anchor: اللهم إن لكل إله حلالا فامنع حلالك لا يغلبن محالهم أبدا محالك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada said Abraha led Ethiopians and Yemeni supporters to destroy the House over a church the Arabs had desecrated; the elephant knelt when turned toward the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: أقبل أبرهة الأشرم بالحبشة ومن تبعه من غواة أهل اليمن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada's account continues: large white birds pelted the army until it became chewed stalks; Abu Yaksum survived, but his flesh fell away as he travelled home and he died.
rows.anchor: بيضا وهي الكبيرة فجعلت ترميهم بها حتى جعلهم الله كعصف مأكول

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identified Abu Yaksum as a tyrant who brought an elephant and Ethiopians to demolish the House over a church destroyed in Yemen; the elephant knelt near the sanctuary but hurried away from it.
rows.anchor: أبو يكسوم جبار من الجبابرة جاء بالفيل يسوقه معه الحبش

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said Abu Yaksum's elephant refused to enter the sanctuary but turned back readily; small white birds then killed the army with chickpea-sized stones.
rows.anchor: فإذا وجه راجعا أسرع راجعا وإذا ارتد على الحرم أبى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas repeated that birds threw black stones coated in clay at the army, whose skin itched and fell away when scratched.
rows.anchor: حجارة سودا عليها الطين فلما حاذت بهم صفت عليهم ثم رمتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said the stones caused smallpox, then a flood swept the army away into the sea; he glossed ababil as separate groups.
rows.anchor: ثم أرسل الله سيلا فذهب بهم فألقاهم في البحر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud glossed ababil as separate groups.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {طيرا أبابيل} قال: هي الفرق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glossed ababil as successive groups of birds arriving from the sea.
rows.anchor: فوجا بعد فوج كانت تخرج عليهم من البحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas described the birds as green, with camel-like beaks and dog-like noses.
rows.anchor: خضر لها خراطيم كخراطيم الإبل وأنف كأنف الكلاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas described the birds as having hands like human hands and teeth like the fangs of beasts.
rows.anchor: لها أكف كأكف الرجل وأنياب كأنياب السباع

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr said swallow-like birds arose from the sea, each carrying three spotted stones; they dropped them from overhead, stones pierced bodies through, and a strong wind helped destroy everyone.
rows.anchor: بكف كل طير منها ثلاثة أحجر مجزعة في منقاره حجر وحجران في رجليه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima described unprecedented white or green birds with beast-like faces whose stones left smallpox-like marks, said to be the first appearance of smallpox.
rows.anchor: طير بيض وفي لفظ: خضر جاءت من قبل البحر كأن وجوهها وجوه السباع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said Abu Yaksum led the attack; ababil means following one another, sijjil means clay, and the spotted agate stones tore them like rotten eaten leaves. The expedition preceded the Prophet's birth by twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: وكانت من جزع أظفار مثل بعر الغنم

rows.speaker: أبو الكنود
rows.claim: Abu al-Kanud said the stones were smaller than a chickpea but larger than a lentil.
rows.anchor: دون الحمصة وفوق العدسة

rows.speaker: عمران
rows.claim: Imran described many birds carrying many stones, ranging from lentil-sized to chickpea-sized.
rows.anchor: طير كثيرة جاءت بحجارة كثيرة أكبرها مثل الحمصة وأصغرها مثل العدسة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, described marked reddish stones like pellets, three for each bird, that encircled and destroyed the army.
rows.anchor: بحجارة مثل البندق وبها نضح حمرة مختمة مع كل طائر ثلاثة أحجار

rows.speaker: نوفل بن معاوية الديلمي
rows.claim: Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya said he had seen the stones, red-marked like Zafar agate and sized between a lentil and a chickpea.
rows.anchor: رأيت الحصى التي رمي بها أصحاب الفيل حصى مثل الحمص وأكبر من العدس

rows.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
rows.claim: Hakim ibn Hizam described red-marked stones the size of chickpeas or lentils; because God used them to punish a people, he would not take one to make a mosque, though they were plentiful in Mecca.
rows.anchor: فلولا أنه عذب به قوم أخذت منه ما اتخذه لي مسجدا وهي بمكة كثير

rows.speaker: أم كرز الخزاعية
rows.claim: Umm Kuraz said she saw the red-marked stones; her account adds that not every member of the army was struck and some escaped.
rows.anchor: رأيت الحجارة التي رمي بها أصحاب الفيل حمرا مختمة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said the army brought two elephants: Mahmud knelt, while the other panicked and was stoned.
rows.anchor: جاؤوا بفيلين فأما محمود فربض وأما الآخر فشجع فحصب

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: A man who spoke to the elephant's commander and driver heard that the Negus's undefeated elephant knelt near the sanctuary despite blows; punishment came, some escaped, and Abraha died after losing limbs on the return journey.
rows.anchor: كلما نوجهه إلى الحرم يربض فتارة نضربه فيهبط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said birds carried one stone in the beak and two in the feet; one stone on a man's head made flesh and blood run off, leaving bare bones.
rows.anchor: تحمل حصاة في منقارها وحصاتين في رجليها ترسل واحدة على رأس الرجل
